summaries.summary: Google Workspace is Google's productivity suite, and a Workspace account can back a Google Cloud Organization resource. It sets the tenant, admin controls and data-region policy (United States, Europe or no preference on qualifying editions), though data regions do not apply to Gemini Notebook data and Gemini coverage is unstated. It is billed per user per month: Business Starter $7, Standard $14, Plus $22; Gemini in Docs starts at Business Standard and AI Expanded Access is a separate add-on.

Google Workspace APIs are Google's REST APIs and extension surfaces for Workspace, including Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Admin SDK, Workspace Events, Apps Script, add-ons and Chat apps. Agents authenticate with OAuth client IDs under user consent, service accounts, or API keys for public data only. Since 2026-05-01 Gmail, Calendar and Drive quotas follow Google's standardized model for agent tools and APIs, and quota increases will require Google Cloud billing.

Google Workspace MCP servers are Google-hosted MCP endpoints for Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Chat, Docs, Sheets and Slides, in Developer Preview and requiring Developer Preview Program membership. They use Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.0; setup means enabling each base API and its MCP service and creating a Web OAuth client marked 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent'. Since 2026-11-11 non-agentic OAuth clients are rejected, and Google warns of prompt injection from untrusted emails and documents.

gpt-6.1-sol is an OpenAI GPT-6 model, shipped 2026-09-29, offering near-Astra quality at lower cost with an April 30 2026 knowledge cutoff. Standard pricing is $2.00 input and $10.00 output per 1M tokens, it supports Ultrafast mode, and it has a 500,000-token default context in Codex. It is a named replacement for gpt-5-family and o3 models shutting down 2026-12-11.

gpt-6-astra is OpenAI's most capable GPT-6 model and the recommended default, shipped 2026-09-03 with an April 30 2026 knowledge cutoff. It brought async tool calling and mid-turn steering to the Responses API and supports Ultrafast mode. Beyond OpenAI's API it is available on Amazon Bedrock in us-west-2 and sold by Azure as a Foundry Model, and it is a recommended Codex model.

gpt-6-luna is OpenAI's most efficient GPT-6 model for high-volume work, shipped 2026-09-22 with a May 18 2026 knowledge cutoff. It is the only model with regional processing for Responses and Chat Completions in Australia, India and Japan (Standard tier, no hosted tools), and is on Amazon Bedrock in us-east-1. It powers the Decisions API (GA 2026-10-22) and replaces several gpt-4o and gpt-4.1 snapshots shutting down 2027-01-14.

Grounding with Google Search is Google's Gemini tool (google_search) that grounds answers in live search results, returning search steps and citation annotations; apps must render the search_suggestions HTML. On Gemini 3+ it bills per executed query, 5,000 free monthly then $14 per 1,000, with a default cap of 1,500 requests per day per project. Query logs are kept up to 3 days with no opt-out, it lacks data residency, CMEK and VPC-SC; Web Grounding for Enterprise is the zero-retention option.

Heroku AppLink, the new name of Heroku Integration, is Salesforce Heroku's service that publishes Heroku apps into Salesforce as External Services, API Catalog entries and Agentforce actions callable from Apex, Flow, Data Cloud and Agentforce. It supports user modes user, user-plus and authorized-user, with Node.js and Python SDKs and a Heroku CLI plugin. The service runs in the virginia region, requires allowlisting AppLink IPs in the org and works only with editions that have API access.

Heroku Managed Inference and Agents is Heroku's add-on (heroku-inference) for model inference and agents, created with heroku addons:create heroku-inference:standard. It offers an agent endpoint at /v1/agents/heroku with tool execution in isolated one-off dynos, and Procfile processes whose names start with mcp register as tools. External MCP clients reach its MCP Toolkit on the /mcp/sse path with the INFERENCE_KEY as Bearer token.

Hyperforce is Salesforce's infrastructure that lets customers choose the region their org runs in, such as the U.S., U.K., Germany, India or Japan, at no extra cost. Customer data is generally stored in the org's country when the services used are available there, though some product components run elsewhere. The paid EU Operating Zone keeps EU customer data stored and processed within the EU, with 24/7 EU-based support.

IAM Unified Access Policies are Google Cloud IAM v3 access policies that govern agent traffic through Agent Gateway, GA since 2026-08-31. They apply allow or deny rules (deny overrides allow; the gateway denies by default) to agent principals, with CEL conditions on tool name, HTTP method or path prefix, bound to the gateway's project. IAP enforces them in DRY_RUN mode, which logs violations to Cloud Audit Logs without blocking, or ENFORCE mode.

Integration Connectors is Google Cloud's managed connector service with 147 connectors (35 Google, 112 third-party), including GA Salesforce, ServiceNow, Snowflake, SharePoint, Workday, Dynamics 365 and SAP; Databricks is not listed. ADK agents use it through ApplicationIntegrationToolset with entity operations and actions. Its MCP connector (preview, v1 and v2) is client-side and allocates 2 nodes per connection by default; exposing a connection as an MCP server is unconfirmed.

The Interactions API is Google's default Gemini API interface (GA June 2026); generateContent is legacy but still supported. It adds server-side state via previous_interaction_id, background mode and observable steps; store defaults to true (55 days paid, 1 day free), and store=false gives zero retention but loses state and background mode. It supports remote MCP over Streamable HTTP only, while Batch, explicit caching and Python automatic function calling remain on generateContent.

InvokeAgentRuntime is the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime data-plane API that invokes agents hosted on AgentCore Runtime, for example from a Lambda function in event-driven patterns. It counts against a shared 1,000 TPS per-account quota. Cross-account calls need allows in resource-based policies on both the agent runtime and its endpoint, and OAuth-authenticated resources must use Principal * with conditions such as aws:SourceVpc or aws:SourceVpce.

IPM Insights is Oracle Cloud EPM's AI feature that detects anomalies, forecast bias and variances with GenAI summaries, first released for Planning in 21.11. It is supported in EPCM, FCCS, FreeForm, Planning, Tax Reporting and Smart View. Release 26.11 added IPM Insights Analysis, insights in dashboards and forms, a REST API for Planning insight details, and the IPM-Manage granular role for access control.

Jules is Google's experimental coding agent, used at jules.google.com after signing in with a Google account and connecting GitHub with access to all or selected repositories. Paid Pro and Ultra tiers are limited to individual @gmail.com accounts, and business users are pointed to an interest form. Limits are 15 tasks per rolling 24 hours (3 concurrent) on Base, 100 (15) on Pro and 300 (60) on Ultra, and a v1alpha REST API exists.

The Jules API is Google's alpha (v1alpha) REST API for the Jules coding agent, described as experimental, with resources for sources, sessions and activities. Sources are GitHub repositories, which need the Jules GitHub app installed. Its status after the Antigravity consolidation and its rate limits are unconfirmed.

Lakebase is Databricks' managed Postgres with branching and Unity Catalog synced tables, GA since 2026-01-22; new instances are Autoscaling projects supporting Postgres 16 to 18 (17 default). Clients authenticate with a one-hour, workspace-scoped Databricks OAuth token as the password over SSL, mapped to a role made with the databricks_auth extension, so pools must refresh tokens. Native password auth is off by default, PgBouncer lacks OAuth support, and Lakebase backs Databricks managed agent memory and sessions.

Managed Environments are Microsoft Power Platform environments with premium governance, entitled by standalone Power Apps, Power Automate, Copilot Studio, Power Pages and Dynamics 365 licenses but not the Developer Plan. They unlock environment groups, sharing limits, IP Firewall, customer-managed keys, Lockbox, pipelines and VNet support, which also needs a linked Azure subscription and VNets in both paired regions. From October 2026, Power Platform pipelines block deployments to unmanaged targets after a 30-day window.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open protocol for connecting agents to tools and data, supported across vendors. Google-managed remote MCP servers are HTTPS endpoints that follow the MCP authorization spec and support version 2026-07-28, and Google's Agent Gateway governs MCP traffic. Microsoft Foundry Toolboxes expose tools through one MCP-compatible endpoint usable by any MCP client, and MuleSoft MCP Connector 1.7 makes Mule apps MCP servers or clients, recommending Streamable HTTP.

MCP Proxy for AWS (mcp-proxy-for-aws) is AWS's open-source, GA proxy that SigV4-signs MCP traffic to AWS-hosted MCP servers and AgentCore Gateway or Runtime endpoints, with read-only mode and retries. It is the SigV4 auth option for the AWS MCP Server, run via uvx with AWS CLI 2.32.0 or later and uv, supporting multiple profiles and a default Region. The current release is 1.8.0 (2026-11-03), and AWS recommends pinning a version.

MCP Toolbox for Databases (formerly genai-toolbox) is Google's open-source MCP server for databases, at v1.17.0 (2026-11-13). It connects agents to AlloyDB, BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Spanner, Firestore and Knowledge Catalog plus PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB, Snowflake and others, via prebuilt toolsets or custom tools in tools.yaml. It runs as a binary, via npx or Go over stdio or HTTP (default port 5000), with client SDKs for Python, JavaScript, Go and Java.

Memory Bank, renamed Agent Platform Memory Bank on 2026-04-22, is Google Cloud's managed agent memory service on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Access is controlled by roles/aiplatform.memoryEditor, memoryUser and memoryViewer. Since 2026-11-06 instances can choose Google-managed or Cloud KMS encryption, though CMEK is not supported on the global endpoint, and residency is tied to the gcp.resourceLocations organization policy (exact conditions unverified).

The Microsoft 365 admin center (admin.microsoft.com / admin.cloud.microsoft) is Microsoft's tenant admin portal where agents are managed under Agents, including the Agent Registry inventory and approval of org-wide agent requests from Copilot Studio, Foundry or the Agents Toolkit. Only Global Administrator and AI Administrator can approve, assign owners, install or modify agents; reader roles are view-only. It also hosts Copilot Credits cost management, and agent settings sync with the Teams admin center.

The Microsoft 365 Agents SDK is Microsoft's multichannel framework for building custom engine conversational agents with any AI service, in C# (.NET 8), JavaScript (Node 18+) and Python. It is an alternative to Direct Line for connecting custom apps to Copilot Studio agents, and since October 2026 Copilot Studio connected agents can target Agents SDK agents. The npm @microsoft/agents-hosting package is at 1.10.1; it is separate from the Microsoft Agent 365 SDK.

Microsoft 365 Copilot is Microsoft's AI assistant add-on for Microsoft 365, requiring a qualifying base license (Microsoft 365 E3/E5, Business or Office 365 plans) except under E7, and offered in GCC, GCC High and DoD. It surfaces only data the user can view, does not train foundation models on prompts, and falls under the DPA and EU Data Boundary. Governance uses Purview audit (CopilotInteraction), sensitivity labels and DLP; extensibility docs now centre on plugins and Work IQ Dev Tools.

Microsoft 365 Copilot APIs are Microsoft Graph REST APIs under the copilot namespace (v1.0 and beta), using standard Entra authentication. As of 2026-11-02 there are nine: Retrieval, Search (preview), Chat (preview), Interaction Export, AI Interactions Change Notifications (preview), Meeting Insights, usage reports, Package Management and Cost Management (preview). They are available only to Copilot-licensed users, and exact Retrieval and Chat paths are unverified.

Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors, formerly Microsoft Graph connectors, bring external content into Microsoft 365 Copilot, with 100+ prebuilt connectors. Synced connectors index content into Graph through the still-named Graph connectors API, while federated connectors fetch live over MCP without indexing and are read-only (write actions announced for October 2026). Connector content is a Retrieval API source, and connector agent registration needs application permissions with tenant-wide admin consent.

The Microsoft 365 Copilot license is Microsoft's per-user add-on at $30 per user per month paid yearly, requiring a qualifying base license such as Microsoft 365 E3/E5/F1/F3, Business plans or Office 365 E1/E3/E5/F3. It includes Work IQ grounding, Copilot in Office apps and Teams, prebuilt agents (Researcher, Analyst, Facilitator) and SharePoint Advanced Management. It also gates developer access: the Copilot APIs, including the Chat API, require Copilot-licensed users.

Microsoft 365 E7 ('Frontier Suite') is Microsoft's enterprise bundle, GA since 2026-05-01, combining Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Entra Suite and Microsoft Agent 365. It removes the need for a separate Copilot add-on and covers the licensing for Conditional Access for agents and agent risk signals. It costs $99 per user per month with annual commitment, or $90.45 without Teams.

Microsoft Agent 365 is Microsoft's control plane for observing, governing and securing AI agents, GA for the Commercial segment since 2026-05-01 and managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center. It extends Entra security (Conditional Access, governance, network controls) to agents, including Copilot Studio agents, and governs BYO MCP servers via the Tools registry. It costs $15 per human user per month standalone, is included in E7 or added to E5 and similar plans, and agent user accounts remain Frontier preview.

The Microsoft Agent 365 SDK is Microsoft's SDK, separate from the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, that adds Entra agent identity, governed Work IQ MCP tooling and notifications to agents built on any framework, including the Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK and LangChain. Microsoft recommends it, with the Agent 365 CLI, for agent identity provisioning and runtime token acquisition. Packages include agents-a365-tooling and framework-specific extensions for npm, Python and .NET.

Microsoft Agent Framework is Microsoft's open-source agent SDK and the direct successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen, with 1.0 GA for .NET and Python on 2026-04-03 and Go in public preview. It covers agents, a Harness Agent, graph-based workflows, MCP clients and providers including Foundry, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama. Packages are agent-framework on PyPI (1.26.0 on 2026-11-12) and Microsoft.Agents.AI on NuGet, and Foundry hosted agents support it.

Microsoft Azure is Microsoft's cloud platform, organized as Entra tenant, root management group, management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and resources, with Azure Resource Manager as control plane. It is bought through MOSP, Enterprise Agreement, Microsoft Customer Agreement or CSP billing accounts. Microsoft Foundry and Azure OpenAI run on it, with Azure OpenAI, AI Search, API Management, Logic Apps, Functions and Copilot Studio in FedRAMP High scope; hashicorp/azurerm is the main Terraform provider.

The Microsoft Copilot harness is a Microsoft agent runtime, in production-ready preview since June 2026, for reasoning-heavy multistep agents in Copilot Studio and Foundry prompt agents, adding skills, per-user memory, file read/write, shell, web, subagents and a sandbox. It is limited to some regions, lacks BYOM, Foundry Memory, store false and previous_response_id, and turns off for FedRAMP High. It bills Copilot Credits from build time, including authoring and testing, and Work IQ in Copilot Studio requires it.

Microsoft Entra is Microsoft's identity product family. Its docs hub lists Entra ID, Entra Agent ID, Workload ID and ID Governance, which together cover identity for human users, workloads and AI agents.

Microsoft Entra Agent ID is Microsoft's GA identity type for AI agents, available to all Entra customers, built on four objects: blueprints (which hold credentials), blueprint principals, agent identities and optional agent user accounts. It adds agent OAuth flows (OBO for interactive, client credentials for autonomous agents), Conditional Access, ID Protection and governance, with security features extended via Agent 365. Copilot Studio and Foundry create agent identities automatically; other app-only platforms are limited to 250 per blueprint.

summaries.key: microsoft entra agent id developer role
summaries.summary: Agent ID Developer is a Microsoft Entra directory role (template adb2368d-a9be-41b5-8667-d96778e081b0) for creating agent identity blueprints and their principals, making the creator owner of both. It is required to create agent identities outside Foundry. Some third-party sources wrongly give it the db506228 template ID, which the authoritative Learn reference assigns to Agent ID Administrator.

A Microsoft Entra agent identity is a special single-tenant service principal created from an agent identity blueprint, which holds the credentials and acquires its tokens. Agent identities start with no permissions, so access must be granted on each downstream resource by object ID; each Foundry hosted agent gets its own. Entra blocks them from highly privileged roles such as Global Administrator and from high-risk Graph permissions (400 Bad Request), and they cannot use OIDC or SAML sign-in.

A Microsoft Entra agent identity blueprint is the Entra Agent ID template that holds credentials and acquires tokens for every agent identity created from it. Permissions, inheritable grants and Conditional Access on a blueprint apply to all its agent identities, and disabling it stops them all authenticating; required resource access is only a declaration. Its only tenant operation is provisioning agent identities via AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager, and Foundry adds a federated credential trusting the Azure Machine Learning app.

AI Administrator is a privileged Microsoft Entra role (template d2562ede-74db-457e-a7b6-544e236ebb61) and the main role for Copilot and agent governance. It manages Copilot, integrated apps and agents, approves line-of-business agents, covers agent identity and blueprint lifecycles, and is needed for Agent Registry Graph endpoints and pinning agents. With Global Administrator it is the only role that can act on agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center; it can edit but not create Copilot Credits spending policies.

A Microsoft Entra app registration defines an application's identity in Entra and is how an engineer's tooling gets Graph access, unless they can request admin consent. Application Developer can create registrations regardless of the 'Users can register applications' setting, while Application Administrator and Cloud Application Administrator manage all registrations and enterprise apps. An app registration can hold at most 20 federated identity credentials when using managed identities as FIC.

Global Administrator is a Microsoft Entra directory role with tenant-wide authority. It is one of two roles that can consent to Graph application permissions and one of two that can act on agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and it can elevate to User Access Administrator at the Azure root management group. It must be assigned directly, no longer auto-receives Power Platform System Administrator, and cannot be assigned to agent identities.

Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft's cloud identity provider, through which all human Azure and Foundry access flows as member or B2B guest principals. Agents calling Foundry, Azure OpenAI or Claude in Foundry use Entra bearer tokens for the ai.azure.com default scope, required for Claude Mythos models. It federates widely: SCIM to AWS IAM Identity Center (direct group members only), Snowflake and Oracle Cloud EPM, SAML SSO, Snowflake External OAuth, and Gemini Enterprise via Workforce Identity Federation.

The Microsoft Entra On-Behalf-Of (OBO) flow lets an interactive agent act for a signed-in user with delegated permissions. Foundry agents can use it as OAuth identity passthrough for MCP and tool connections, Foundry MCP Server uses it, and it is the default outgoing auth strategy for remote Azure MCP Server. Work IQ supports OBO but not app-only auth.

Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium is Microsoft's paid SKU, listed at $3 per workload identity per month, adding Conditional Access and ID Protection for workload identities, access reviews and app health recommendations. Conditional Access applies only to single-tenant service principals, not managed identities. Managed identities and workload identity federation remain free.

Microsoft Entra workload identity federation lets a user-assigned managed identity or app registration trust tokens from external OIDC issuers and exchange them for Entra access tokens with no stored secret. Supported sources include GitHub Actions, any Kubernetes cluster (including EKS and GKE), Google Cloud, AWS via IAM Outbound Identity Federation, SPIFFE/SPIRE and Azure Pipelines. Entra-issued tokens cannot be the external token, and Entra caches only the first 100 issuer signing keys.

Microsoft Fabric is Microsoft's analytics platform, organized into workspaces with Admin, Member, Contributor and Viewer roles; only Admin can create a workspace identity or connect Git. Entra service principals can hold workspace roles, subject to Fabric admin settings: calling public APIs is enabled by default for new customers, while creating workspaces, connections and pipelines is disabled by default. Viewing Power BI content with a Free license needs F64 capacity or larger.

Microsoft Fabric data agents are GA Fabric agents that answer natural-language questions over lakehouses, warehouses, Power BI semantic models, KQL databases, mirrored databases, ontologies and Microsoft Graph by generating SQL, DAX and KQL. They need F2+ or P1+ capacity, run read-only under the requesting user's identity, and fail if data source and agent capacities are in different regions. Limits: 5 data sources, 25 rows by 25 columns per answer, English-only, no unstructured files, fixed LLM.

Microsoft Foundry (renamed from Azure AI Foundry in November 2025) is Microsoft's Azure platform for models and agents, including Claude and OpenAI models. Access uses Entra ID, recommended over API keys; the least-privilege developer role is Foundry User, assigned to developers and the project managed identity (automatically only via the portal), and Cognitive Services roles should be avoided except Usages Reader for quota. Network isolation is constrained: outbound VNet injection is fixed at creation and several tools are unsupported.

A Microsoft Foundry resource (ARM type Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts) is the top-level administrative, security and monitoring boundary in Microsoft Foundry, with projects as sub-scopes. Public network access can be disabled (private endpoint only, sub-resource 'account' with a privatelink DNS zone), limited to selected IPs, or open to all networks. A restricted resource can still admit trusted services Microsoft.CognitiveServices, Microsoft.Search and Microsoft.MachineLearningServices whose managed identities hold the right role.

Microsoft Graph is Microsoft's API for Microsoft 365 and Entra data, governed by Entra directory roles and permissions, and home to the Copilot APIs under its copilot namespace. Delegated permissions are bounded by the user's access, so agents should prefer narrow delegated (OBO) scopes and reserve application permissions for background agents with Selected or OwnedBy constraints. The global throttle is 130,000 requests per 10 seconds per app, returning 429 with Retry-After, and throttled batch items are not auto-retried.

Microsoft Graph application permissions (app roles) give an app access to all data the permission covers and require admin consent. Only Privileged Role Administrator and Global Administrator can grant that consent. Graph connector agents must use application permissions with tenant-wide admin consent, since delegated permissions are not supported for connector agent registration.

The Microsoft Learn MCP Server is Microsoft's free, unauthenticated remote MCP server for Microsoft documentation, served over Streamable HTTP on Microsoft Learn's api/mcp path; a browser GET returning 405 is expected. Its tools are microsoft_docs_search, microsoft_docs_fetch and microsoft_code_sample_search, and its index refreshes incrementally and fully once a day.

The Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise is Microsoft's preview remote MCP server, linked from the Graph docs, giving agents read-only access to Microsoft Entra directory data. Its tools are microsoft_graph_suggest_queries, microsoft_graph_get and microsoft_graph_list_properties. It costs nothing extra, allows 100 calls per minute per user and runs in the global cloud only.

Model Armor is Google Cloud's service that screens prompts and responses for prompt injection and jailbreaks, sensitive data, malicious URLs, RAI categories and CSAM, with floor settings enforcing project-wide minimums, billed on tokens screened. Agent Gateway enforces it on agent traffic, and it integrates with Gemini Enterprise, Agent Runtime, Google Cloud MCP servers and Apigee API hub. It is unavailable in the Gemini Enterprise global location, and console settings don't protect registered ADK or A2A agents, which need REST configuration.
